speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a scalp and forehead rash; to help me understand your condition, can you describe exactly what the rash looks like and when it started?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given the 3-month-old age, history of cold exposure, and scaly red appearance, could you specify if the rash is primarily on the cheeks or involves the scalp, and are there any areas that appear shiny or hairless?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap)
